      About the tracker and its method

      China–Azerbaijan Investment Tracker is a register of investment in Azerbaijan by mainland Chinese, Hong Kong and Macau firms and Chinese-owned foreign brands, built from the Azerbaijani-language press. It extends the China–Turkey Investment Tracker, the China–Hungary Investment Tracker and the China–Kazakhstan Investment Tracker to Azerbaijan, the Caspian crossing of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (Middle Corridor) between Kazakhstan and Georgia, with the same unit (a project), the same evidence (one claim per article, quoted word for word and linked) and the same reading of outcomes, and it keeps the registry checks of Gürel, Selamet, Şahinli, Sen and Tuzcu (2026), Asian Perspective 50(2): 219–257. Compiled by Osman Demirbağ, Burak Gürel, Kadir Selamet. Data release 2026-10-31.

      Definitions used on the first screen

      The headline, the squares and the four further findings use these terms. Counts follow the settings chosen above the squares (currently ).

      Realised
      Operating, under construction or acquired, as last reported.
      Live promise
      Announced, agreed, in talks or rumoured, with a press report found within the last .
      Dormant promise
      No press report found for or more ( projects at 2 / 3 / 5 years). This is not a confirmed cancellation: rest on a single press report.
      Failed or exited
      A bid lost or not made (), a promise abandoned or put on hold (), or an exit after realisation, by closure or sale ().
      Promise phase
      First reported as interest, talks, a bid or a promise: of the investment projects. The promise-phase base counts only these; projects that entered the press already realised, such as completed acquisitions, have no promise phase on record.
      Chinese
      Includes Hong Kong and Macau firms and Chinese-owned brands. Mainland firms alone: realised. Taiwanese firms are excluded.
      Not counted
      non-equity or contractor and finance items: kept in the register and the explorer, not counted as investment.

      How the register was built

      The register follows the Turkey tracker's design and the three search stages of the Hungary tracker, so that firms nobody named in advance and reports that name no firm are caught as well. Every step leaves a file in the project repository, and every number on this page is computed from those files.

      1. Stage 1, known firms. 111 Chinese, Hong Kong and Macau firms and Chinese-owned brands, plus 33 names found later, searched under 214 terms in the search pages of 8 Azerbaijani sites and in the article addresses listed by the sitemaps of 5 more.
      2. Stage 2, every China-related investment story. 28 Azerbaijani queries such as Çin şirkəti, Çinli investor or Azərbaycan-Çin birgə in the same site searches, and the sitemap addresses whose words name China.
      3. Stage 3, registries and China's own list. The GLEIF register of legal entities (77 Azerbaijani records), and the main Chinese investors named by China's Ministry of Commerce in its country guide for Azerbaijan.
      4. Fetch. Pages downloaded at a polite rate, text extracted, and every sentence naming a seed firm or China next to investment vocabulary kept as a candidate.
      5. Curation. 12 curation passes turned the candidates into projects and claims, each claim with the verbatim Azerbaijani sentence, an English translation and the link; a script rejected any quote not found word for word in the downloaded article.
      6. Feedback. Names found by the curators and in stage 2 went back into stage 1 and were searched in the same way.

      Sources

      Google News, the search behind the Hungarian register, holds few Azerbaijani-language articles. Both search stages therefore query the sites' own search pages: the news agency Trend, the state daily Xalq qəzeti, Azərbaycan (the daily of the National Assembly), the pro-government daily İki sahil, the business sites Marja.az, İqtisadiyyat.az and Banker.az, and President.az, the official site of the President. Each matches words anywhere in an article's text; Trend (its first 24 results), İki sahil, İqtisadiyyat.az and President.az serve only the first page of results. Report.az, Oxu.az, AzerTac, the state news agency, and 525-ci qəzet answer scripted requests with HTTP 403 behind a firewall; the search pages of Azadlıq Radiosu (the Azerbaijani service of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty), Axar, Teleqraf, Sia, Publika, Səs, Fed.az and Yeni Müsavat are disallowed in their robots.txt, which the pipeline respects; APA loads its results by script. Five sites whose articles and sitemaps are open are searched through their sitemaps instead: the words of every article address, a transliteration of the headline, are matched (Qafqazinfo from 2014, Meydan TV from 2013, Modern.az from 2009, Fed.az, and Lent.az, whose sitemap lists recent articles only). AzerTac reports enter the register only as carried by other outlets.

      The source list (config/sources.csv) names 35 sources: news agencies (4): Trend, APA, Report.az, AzerTac; national dailies (7): Xalq qəzeti, Azərbaycan, İki sahil, 525-ci qəzet, Səs, Müsavat, Yeni Müsavat; business news (4): Marja.az, İqtisadiyyat.az, Banker.az, Fed.az; official sources (6): President.az, Ministry of Economy, AZPROMO, Alat Free Economic Zone, Sumgait Chemical Industrial Park, SOCAR; national news (10): Qafqazinfo, Modern.az, Lent.az, Oxu.az, Azadlıq Radiosu, Axar.az, Teleqraf, Sia.az, Publika.az, Azvision; independent outlets (1): Meydan TV; international broadcasters (1): BBC Azərbaycanca; registries (1): GLEIF; Chinese official sources (1): MOFCOM country guide. State media (Xalq qəzeti, Azərbaycan, President.az) and the agencies carry most announcements, agreements and openings; Meydan TV and Azadlıq Radiosu report more of the conflicts (labour, land, environment, debts). Claims by type of outlet: business news 145, national dailies 130, news agencies 113, national news 19, official sources 13, other outlets 6, independent outlets 3. Most cited: Trend (112), Azərbaycan (110), Marja.az (75), Banker.az (39), Fed.az (30), İki sahil (18), Qafqazinfo (11), President.az (9), Ministry of Economy (4), Modern.az (4).

      Stage 1: known Chinese firms

      The seed list holds 111 firms in three groups: 23 reported present in Azerbaijan (the firms named in the MOFCOM country guide, among them its list of the main Chinese enterprises, and in the Azerbaijani press), 45 present in Georgia, Central Asia, Turkey or Russia and 43 global majors whose presence in Azerbaijan was to be checked. 33 names were added after the first curation.

      Each name was searched in all 8 site searches, up to ten pages per term and site, and in the article addresses of the 5 sitemap indexes. The Azerbaijani press writes Chinese firm names in Latin letters, often in quotation marks with the ending after a hyphen (“BYD”-nin), and translates the names of state-owned groups (Çin Yol və Körpü Korporasiyası). Because the site searches match a name anywhere in an article, the headline and lead decide what is downloaded: for firms known in Azerbaijan they must name the firm or carry investment or China vocabulary (a Yutong bus in a road accident is not a Yutong story), for the others the firm next to investment or Azerbaijan vocabulary, or China next to investment vocabulary. Azerbaijani place names alone do not count, as nearly every headline has one. Sitemap addresses are read the same way from their words.

      Azerbaijani attaches case and possessive endings to names. A foreign or abbreviated name takes them after a hyphen, an apostrophe or the closing quotation mark (“Huawei”-in, BYD-nin, ÇXR-in); a name written as an Azerbaijani word takes them straight on (Çinin, Sinopekin). As the endings use the same Latin letters as the names, the matcher accepts a direct ending only from a list of Azerbaijani case and derivational endings, so that Gree does not match Green; short names and abbreviations take endings only after a hyphen or apostrophe.

      Stage 2: every China-related investment story

      Generic Azerbaijani queries catch firms that were not on the list and reports that name no firm at all (“Çin şirkəti …”). 28 queries, up to thirty pages each in every site search, and a scan of the sitemap addresses for words naming China returned 7,825 results, of which 1,872 had China (or a seed firm) and investment vocabulary in the headline, lead or address and were downloaded. Of the downloaded stage-2 articles, 812 carry a China-and-investment sentence tied to an Azerbaijani place.

      Stage 2 and the curators' feedback round added 46 projects that the seed list had not reached, and 91 general signals: investment totals, unnamed investors, delegations and policy reviews.

      Stage 3: registries and China's own list

      No country list in Azerbaijan. In Turkey, the ministry's list of foreign-capital firms gives each firm's country, and the Asian Perspective article checked it against the trade-registry gazette and the central registry. Azerbaijan publishes no such list: the state register of legal entities (Ministry of Taxes, e-taxes.gov.az) answers one taxpayer identification number (VÖEN) at a time and does not show owners.

      GLEIF. The open register of legal entity identifiers holds only 77 Azerbaijani entities (Hungary has more than 26,000): identifiers are needed mainly by banks and bond issuers. Screening their parents and names found no entity with a Chinese, Hong Kong or Macau parent or a Chinese firm's name. GLEIF is a floor here, much more than in Hungary.

      China's own list. China's Ministry of Commerce names, in its country guide for outward investors (对外投资合作国别（地区）指南·阿塞拜疆, 2025 edition), the main Chinese enterprises in Azerbaijan (appendix 2). Of its 21 names, 20 were on the seed list; 10 are now covered by projects in the register. Not covered: North Hengtai Technology Development, Beijing Huayou Oil and Gas Technology Development, Shandong Kerui Petroleum Equipment, Azerbaijan office, Sichuan Honghua Petroleum Equipment, representative office, Xinjiang Jinmanda International Trade, representative office, Huanyu International LLC, Baku Keshla steel plant, Argonavt LLC, Zhejiang Dahua Technology, Baku Great Wall Hotel (restaurant), Baku Chinese hotpot restaurant. According to the guide, Chinese firms signed 17 new construction and engineering contracts in Azerbaijan in 2024, worth about USD 970 million.

      What the statistics say. China's Ministry of Commerce puts China's direct investment stock in Azerbaijan at USD 16.99 million at the end of 2024. The Central Bank of Azerbaijan, as cited in the same guide, records USD 7.05 billion of foreign direct investment inflows in 2024, mostly into oil and gas; China is not among the ten largest sources (the United Kingdom, Turkey, Hungary, Cyprus, the United Arab Emirates, Iran, Japan, Russia, the United States and Norway). In Azerbaijan, Chinese construction contracts (17 new contracts worth about USD 970 million in 2024, by the same guide) and loans weigh far more than Chinese equity. Neither figure shows Chinese capital held through third jurisdictions such as the Netherlands, Cyprus, Singapore or Luxembourg. This is why the register records holding routes where they are documented (1 projects; Hong Kong 1).

      Downloading and reading the articles

      The pages were downloaded directly at a polite rate (one request every one and a half seconds per site, shared by all workers and by the search and download processes). 4,640 articles were downloaded: 3,106 from stage 1, 1,519 from stage 2 and 15 added by the curators; 4,572 came with their full text from 21 domains.

      The texts were split into 137,296 sentences. A sentence became a candidate when it named a seed firm or China (Çin, çinli, ÇXR, Honkonq …) next to investment vocabulary (investisiya, zavod, müəssisə, səhm, milyard …): 14,677 sentences in 3,601 articles, 5,899 of them naming a seed firm. Each candidate carries a lifecycle tier from ordered Azerbaijani keyword rules (failure, other, realisation, interest, promise).

      Curation: from articles to projects and claims

      A project is a firm, or an identifiable investor, tied to a site or a target in Azerbaijan; separate sites, stakes and separately reported phases are separate projects. A claim is one article and one step: the Azerbaijani sentence copied character for character, its English translation, the article link, the date, the outlet and the step's label. Reports of Chinese interest that cannot be tied to a firm or site are general signals.

      The passes were merged by a script that checks every field and value and rejects a quote that does not occur word for word in the downloaded text (an ellipsis may mark an omission). 426 of the 429 claims were matched this way; 0 quote Russian-language, 0 Turkish-language and 3 English-language reports because no Azerbaijani report of that step was found, and 7 quote only a headline or a lead. 0 projects curated twice were folded into one and 13 field changes were made after later reports; each decision is recorded with its reason. The curators logged 66 leads for follow-up.

      The English translations were written during curation, each next to its verbatim Azerbaijani sentence; the field translation_method records how each was made.

      Claim types: 323 investment steps (plan, agreement, investment contract, resident status in an industrial park or the free economic zone, land allocation, groundbreaking, opening, acquisition, expansion, exit), 32 mentions in passing, 3 company news (fines, accidents, labour disputes, protests) and 71 contractor or finance items. Lifecycle tiers: 135 promise, 126 interest, 63 realisation, 6 failure and 99 other.

      What was filtered out, and why

      1. At the search stage, results were kept for download only when the headline or lead carried the vocabulary described above: 16,465 of 22,403 results were set aside. Some search terms are also ordinary words or match by stem, so most of their results were set aside: Transsion / Oppo / Vivo / Honor / Realme (phones) (533 results, 47 kept).
      2. At the reading stage, only sentences with a firm or China term next to investment vocabulary became candidates (14,677 of 137,296 sentences).
      3. Not Chinese. Taiwanese firms are excluded, and so are Turkish, Russian, Korean, Iranian and Western firms named next to a Chinese one unless a Chinese firm takes part in the step.
      4. Not investment. Chinese brands assembled or sold under licence by Azerbaijani firms (Ganja Automobile Plant, Nakhchivan Automobile Plant, dealers) are non-equity presence unless Chinese equity is reported, and so are air and cargo routes, licences, consortia, technology partnerships and memoranda without a Chinese stake; construction contracts, Chinese loans, export credit and credit lines are contractor or finance items. None of them is counted as investment.
      5. Searched, but nothing in Azerbaijan. Names with the most candidate articles and no project:

      Coding choices to review

      • Sites, stakes and phases that the press reports separately are separate projects: a factory in the Sumgait Chemical Industrial Park and a second one in the Alat Free Economic Zone are two projects.
      • Joint ventures with the state (SOCAR, Azerenerji, Azerbaijan Investment Holding, Azerbaijan Railways, AzerGold, AzerAluminium) are investment when the Chinese side holds equity; the Azerbaijani partner is recorded.
      • Industrial parks and the free economic zone: a resident of an industrial park or of the Alat Free Economic Zone with a Chinese owner is a new facility, and the park or zone is recorded as state support.
      • Purchases abroad: a Chinese-owned foreign brand or a company bought abroad (Volvo Cars of Geely, Pirelli of ChemChina) counts when its Azerbaijani unit is reported.
      • Licence assembly: Chinese brands assembled or sold under licence by Azerbaijani firms (Ganja Automobile Plant, Nakhchivan Automobile Plant, dealers) are non-equity presence for the Chinese brand unless Chinese equity is reported.
      • Loans and contracts (EPC contracts, loans of China Development Bank, Exim Bank of China or Bank of China, export credit, credit lines) are kept as contractor or finance items, not as investment.
      • Origin not established for 0 projects whose owners are described only as Chinese investors.

      Stages, outcomes, figures and the map

      Stages and outcomes

      Each project carries the stage it reached as last reported: realised or under way, agreed or announced, interest, talks or a bid, rumour, failed, lost or exited, non-equity presence, and contractor or finance only. The site reads the stage together with the time since the last report, as the Turkey tracker does. Realised and failed follow the stage. Announced, agreed, in-talks or rumoured projects are live promises while a report falls inside the dormancy window and dormant promises once none has been found for that long (three years by default; two and five are offered). A dormant promise means that no evidence of progress was found, not that the project was cancelled. A non-equity arrangement or a contract or loan is never counted as investment, even when its stage records that it ended.

      Claims and lifecycle tiers

      Each claim has a lifecycle tier read from its event label with ordered rules: failure words first, then later references and denials as “other”, then realisation, commitment and interest; resident status in an industrial park or the Alat Free Economic Zone counts as a commitment. The first realisation-tier claim dates a realisation, the first failure-tier claim a failure, and the first claim's tier records how the press first found the project. The time-to-outcome chart estimates the cumulative incidence of realisation and failure for projects first reported as interest or a promise (Aalen–Johansen), treating projects still open at the release as censored.

      Reported figures

      32 projects report a headline figure. Each was read by hand and classed by what it measures: 10 pledge, 9 contract finance, 7 project cost, 5 registered capital, 1 invested. Only announced pledges are compared across outcomes (10 projects). Manat, yuan, euro and rouble figures are converted to US dollars at the World Bank's annual average rate of the year the figure was reported (the latest published year for later years), so that they sit on the Turkey tracker's scale; a figure in old manats, which the new manat replaced at 5,000 to one in 2006, is first converted to new manats. Figures are as announced and not verified.

      The map

      Regions are the 14 economic regions of the 2021 division, Baku among them, coded from the site named in the articles; a site reported before 2021 is coded by its region in the 2021 division. A project with sites in several regions is counted in each, and 64 projects with no reported region are listed under “No region reported”. Outlines: each economic region is the union of its districts and cities as grouped in the 2021 division, from the district outlines of geoBoundaries (drawn from Wikipedia's map of the districts, CC BY-SA 3.0; their borders are approximate); Nakhchivan is shown as the exclave it is, and the Mingachevir and Shamkir reservoirs as water. Neighbouring countries from Eurostat GISCO and lakes from Natural Earth; Lambert conformal conic projection with standard parallels at 39°N and 41.5°N.

      The first screen and the explorer

      The headline, the squares and the four further findings describe all investment projects as last reported, on the comparison base and dormancy threshold chosen there; explorer filters do not change them, they highlight the matching projects. Outcome, sector, origin and form filters are inclusive within a group and combine across groups. A link to any view can be copied from the results bar, and each project opens its evidence timeline with the Azerbaijani quotes, their translations and links to the articles.

      Limits

      This is a register of press reports, not of capital flows. A promise can be realised without the press noticing, and a realised project may have had a promise phase no archive captured. The archives reach back unevenly: of the sitemaps, Modern.az's start in 2009, Meydan TV's in 2013 and Qafqazinfo's in 2014, and Lent.az's list only recent articles; four site searches serve only their first page of results. Report.az, Oxu.az, AzerTac and 525-ci qəzet could not be read and APA could not be searched, so their reports enter the register only as carried by other outlets or found otherwise; Russian-, Turkish- and English-language reports are quoted only where no Azerbaijani report of a step was found. The state register answers one taxpayer number (VÖEN) at a time and does not show owners, so the owners and stakes of Azerbaijani companies rest on press reports, company disclosures and GLEIF; the evidence for each attribution is named in the curation notes of the project. Recent cohorts are right-censored, and some associations are built into the data: holding routes are documented mostly once a company exists, and a named region is itself a sign of progress. Treat such differences as descriptive.
